fanoutqa_000205.x:
Star Wars: The Force Awakens :: Reception :: Box office :: Commercial analysis :: chunk_0023
Analysts said that the box office receipts of the film, when compared to predecessors, must be adjusted for inflation, and that the first *Star Wars* film made more when this adjustment is made.[[299]](#cite_note-Stock-304) It has further been observed that each of the first three films in the series was more profitable in calculating revenue against production costs.[[299]](#cite_note-Stock-304)

While *The Force Awakens* was very successful in the United States and Canada, the same success was not witnessed in many overseas individual markets such as India, other certain parts of Asia and Latin America. This was attributed to it being "a retro film" and how overseas audiences do not have the same nostalgia or affinity for the film as those in North America.[[300]](#cite_note-McClintock-305)[[301]](#cite_note-Eggertse-306)[[302]](#cite_note-Tartaglione-307) The *Star Wars* franchise has traditionally lacked resonance with filmgoers in China, and marketing for *The Force Awakens* heavily focused on appealing to that market.[[301]](#cite_note-Eggertse-306)[[303]](#cite_note-Tartaglione2-308)

Nancy Tartaglione of *Deadline Hollywood* argued that, if accounting for its 40/60 domestic to international split, *The Force Awakens* did well overseas.[[302]](#cite_note-Tartaglione-307) While the film had special effects, analysts felt that it lacked the novelty factor; they also stated that its gross was stilted due to markets making way for new films sooner than was previously done.[[301]](#cite_note-Eggertse-306) Dergarabedian stated, "No matter what, [*The Force Awakens*] is an absolute, all-out blockbuster without peer in terms of the sheer speed at which it has crossed all of these major box-office milestones."[[300]](#cite_note-McClintock-305) Moreover, Mike Fleming Jr. of *Deadline Hollywood* argued that the movie was the "most valuable movie" of the year, with "the net profi

With 28 Olympic medals (23 of them gold), he is the most decorated Olympian of all time.

The United States has hosted the modern Olympic Games eight times, more than any other nation. These occasions span from the 1904 St. Louis Olympics to the 2002 Salt Lake City Winter Olympics. Beyond hosting, the U.S. has significantly impacted the Olympics through athletic achievements, innovations in sports infrastructure and technology, and cultural contributions. Its influence extends to advocating Olympic ideals and leaving lasting legacies in host cities. Overall, the U.S. plays a central role in the history and ongoing development of the Olympic movement. For example, the 1932 Los Angeles Olympics pioneered the use of electronic timing devices. The 1984 Los Angeles Olympics, for instance, set new standards for opening and closing ceremonies. Even when not hosting, the U.S. has played a crucial role in the administration and promotion of the Olympics through organizations like the [United States Olympic Committee](/wiki/United_States_Olympic_Committee "United States Olympic Committee") (USOC) and its participation in the [International Olympic Committee](/wiki/International_Olympic_Committee "International Olympic Committee") (IOC). Premier League :: Corporate structure :: chunk_0009
The Football Association Premier League Ltd (FAPL)[[64]](#cite_note-66)[[65]](#cite_note-67)[[66]](#cite_note-68) is operated as a corporation and is owned by the 20 member clubs. Each club is a [shareholder](/wiki/Shareholder "Shareholder"), with one vote each on issues such as rule changes and contracts. The clubs select a chairman, chief executive, and board of directors to oversee the daily operations of the league.[[67]](#cite_note-69) The Football Association is not directly involved in the day-to-day operations of the Premier League, but has veto power as a special shareholder during the election of the chairman and chief executive and when new rules are adopted by the league.[[68]](#cite_note-70)

The current chief executive is [Richard Masters](/wiki/Richard_Masters_(football) "Richard Masters (football)"), who was appointed in December 2019.[[69]](#cite_note-71) The chair is currently [Alison Brittain](/wiki/Alison_Brittain "Alison Brittain"), who took over the role in early 2023.[[70]](#cite_note-72)

The Premier League sends representatives to UEFA's [European Club Association](/wiki/European_Club_Association "European Club Association"), the number of clubs and the clubs themselves chosen according to [UEFA coefficients](/wiki/UEFA_coefficient "UEFA coefficient"). For the [2023–24 season](/wiki/2023%E2%80%9324_Premier_League "2023–24 Premier League"), the Premier League has 13 representatives in the Association: Arsenal, Aston Villa, [Brighton & Hove Albion](/wiki/Brighton_%26_Hove_Albion_F.C. fanoutqa_039373.x:
Philip H. Dybvig :: Career :: chunk_0001
Dybvig attended [Indiana University](/wiki/Indiana_University "Indiana University") and received in 1976 a BA in mathematics and physics. He then attended the economics PhD program at [University of Pennsylvania](/wiki/University_of_Pennsylvania "University of Pennsylvania") for one year before transferring to [Yale University](/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University"), where he received the MA (1978), MPhil (1978), and PhD (1979) degrees in economics.[[3]](#cite_note-CV-3) His thesis, titled "Recovering additive utility functions", was supervised by [Stephen A. Ross](/wiki/Stephen_A._Ross "Stephen A. Ross").[[4]](#cite_note-4)

Dybvig specializes in [asset pricing](/wiki/Asset_pricing "Asset pricing"), banking, investments, and [corporate governance](/wiki/Corporate_governance "Corporate governance").[[5]](#cite_note-Olin_Faculty-5) He was formerly a professor at [Yale University](/wiki/Yale_University "Yale University"), and assistant professor at [Princeton University](/wiki/Princeton_University "Princeton University").

Dybvig was president of the [Western Finance Association](/wiki/Western_Finance_Association "Western Finance Association") from 2002 to 2003, and was director of the Institute of Financial Studies at [Southwestern University of Finance and Economics](/wiki/Southwestern_University_of_Finance_and_Economics "Southwestern University of Finance and Economics") ([Chengdu](/wiki/Chengdu "Chengdu"), [PRC](/wiki/PRC "PRC")) from 2010 to 2021. He has been editor or associate editor of multiple journals, including the *Journal of Economic Theory*, *Finance and Stochastics*, *Journal of Finance*, *Journal of Financial Intermediation*, *Journal of Financial and Quantitative Analysis*, and *Review of Financial Studies*.[[3]](#cite_note-CV-3)

Dybvig is known for his work with [Douglas Diamond](/wiki/Douglas_Diamond "Douglas Diamond") on the [Diamond–Dybvig model](/wiki/Diamond%E2%80%93Dybvig_model "Diamond–Dybvig model")

See also: [List of megathrust earthquakes](/wiki/List_of_megathrust_earthquakes "List of megathrust earthquakes")

Great earthquakes such as the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake are generally associated with [megathrust](/wiki/Megathrust_earthquake "Megathrust earthquake") events in [subduction](/wiki/Subduction "Subduction") zones. Their [seismic moments](/wiki/Seismic_moment "Seismic moment") can account for a significant fraction of the global seismic moment across century-scale periods. Of all the moment released by earthquakes in the 100 years from 1906 through 2005, roughly one-eighth was due to the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake.[[35]](#cite_note-:0-36) This quake, together with the [Great Alaskan earthquake](/wiki/1964_Alaska_earthquake "1964 Alaska earthquake") (1964) and the [Great Chilean earthquake](/wiki/1960_Valdivia_earthquake "1960 Valdivia earthquake") (1960), account for almost half of the total moment.[[35]](#cite_note-:0-36)[[36]](#cite_note-37)

Since 1900, the only earthquakes recorded with a greater magnitude were the 1960 Chile earthquake (magnitude 9.5) and the 1964 Alaska earthquake in [Prince William Sound](/wiki/Prince_William_Sound "Prince William Sound") (magnitude 9.2). The only other recorded earthquakes of magnitude 9.0 or greater were off [Kamchatka, Russia, in November 1952](/wiki/1952_Severo-Kurilsk_earthquake "1952 Severo-Kurilsk earthquake") (magnitude 9.0) and [Tōhoku, Japan, in March 2011](/wiki/2011_T%C5%8Dhoku_earthquake_and_tsunami "2011 Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami") (magnitude 9.1). Each of these megathrust earthquakes also spawned tsunamis in the Pacific Ocean. In comparison to the 2004 Indian Ocean earthquake, the death toll from these earthquakes and tsunamis was significantly lower, primarily because of the lower population density along the coasts near affected areas.[[8]](#cite_note-:1-8)

The United Kingdom's topography

[England](/wiki/Geography_of_England "Geography of England") accounts for 53 per cent of the UK, covering 50,350 square miles (130,395 km2).[[147]](#cite_note-165) Most of the country consists of lowland terrain,[[148]](#cite_note-Atlapedia-166) with upland and mountainous terrain northwest of the [Tees–Exe line](/wiki/Tees%E2%80%93Exe_line "Tees–Exe line") which roughly divides the UK into [lowland and upland](/wiki/Lowland_and_upland "Lowland and upland") areas. Lowland areas include [Cornwall](/wiki/Cornwall "Cornwall"), the [New Forest](/wiki/New_Forest "New Forest"), the [South Downs](/wiki/South_Downs "South Downs") and the [Norfolk Broads](/wiki/The_Broads "The Broads"). Upland areas include the [Lake District](/wiki/Lake_District "Lake District"), the [Pennines](/wiki/Pennines "Pennines"), the [Yorkshire Dales](/wiki/Yorkshire_Dales "Yorkshire Dales"), [Exmoor](/wiki/Exmoor "Exmoor") and [Dartmoor](/wiki/Dartmoor "Dartmoor"). The main rivers and estuaries are the [Thames](/wiki/River_Thames "River Thames"), [Severn](/wiki/River_Severn "River Severn"), and the [Humber](/wiki/Humber "Humber"). England's highest mountain is [Scafell Pike](/wiki/Scafell_Pike "Scafell Pike"), at 978 metres (3,209 ft) in the Lake District; its largest island is the [Isle of Wight](/wiki/Isle_of_Wight "Isle of Wight").

[Scotland](/wiki/Geography_of_Scotland "Geography of Scotland") accounts for 32 per cent of the UK, covering 30,410 square miles (78,772 km2).[[149]](#cite_note-167) This includes [nearly 800 islands](/wiki/List_of_islands_of_Scotland "List of islands of Scotland"),[[150]](#cite_note-168) notably the [Hebrides](/wiki/Hebrides "Hebrides"), [Orkney](/wiki/Orkney "Orkney") Islands and [Shetland Islands](/wiki/Shetland_Islands "Shetland Islands"). Jennifer Aniston :: Acting credits and awards :: chunk_0014
Main articles: [Jennifer Aniston filmography](/wiki/Jennifer_Aniston_filmography "Jennifer Aniston filmography") and [List of awards and nominations received by Jennifer Aniston](/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Jennifer_Aniston "List of awards and nominations received by Jennifer Aniston")

Aniston received five Primetime Emmy Award nominations, two Golden Globe Award nominations, and nine SAG Award nominations for her role in *Friends*. From these, she won one of each. She also garnered a Primetime Emmy Award nomination for her guest appearance in *30 Rock*, while her performance in *Cake* earned her nominations at the Golden Globe and SAG awards. Aniston additionally won a SAG Award and was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award and a Golden Globe Award for the first season of *The Morning Show*, and earned multiple nominations at Critics' Choice, Golden Globe, Primetime Emmy and SAG awards for its subsequent seasons. As a producer, she was nominated for a Primetime Emmy Award and three Golden Globe Awards.

According to review aggregator site [Rotten Tomatoes](/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes") and the box-office site [Box Office Mojo](/wiki/Box_Office_Mojo "Box Office Mojo"), Aniston's most critically acclaimed and commercially successful films are *Office Space* (1999), *The Good Girl* (2002), *Bruce Almighty* (2003), *Friends with Money* (2006), *The Break-Up* (2006), *Marley & Me* (2008), *Just Go with It* (2011), *Horrible Bosses* (2011), *We're the Millers* (2013), and *Dumplin'* (2018).[[220]](#cite_note-222)[[47]](#cite_note-highest_gross-47)
